title: 11 real published documents, 34 known molecules — all three stages
corpus: 11 PDFs as published: 3 patents, 5 journal papers, 3 government reports
corpus_detail: Assembled for DRAWING-STYLE diversity, which is the variable the earlier corpora hold constant: ChemDraw vector typesetting, a 1980 USPTO hand-inked scan, an EPO B1 hybrid of vector text and 300-dpi clippings, genuinely hand-drawn structures scanned off paper, raster crops of patent images, and vector line art in two-column government reports. Every PDF is the publisher's own file, committed with its licence and a SHA-256 checksum. Ground truth is the molecules the document NAMES that resolve to a PubChem CID — 34 across the 11 — each one located by page and pixel-verified against PubChem's depiction of that CID. The documents draw far more compounds than that: synthesis intermediates, Markush skeletons and reagents with no reference to score against.
stages: All three: VisualHeist figure extraction, DECIMER segmentation, then CXMolScribe. 73 figures, 242 structures.
method: RDKit canonical SMILES on both sides, never string equality. Every prediction is scored under FOUR comparisons — the CXSMILES exactly as predicted, that string's largest fragment, the string with its abbreviations expanded, and both — and the ladder of all four is shown so a visitor can see which step moved which number. Recall is counted per document against the molecules drawn in THAT document, then summed; the 11 per-document manifests are the denominators. Abbreviations are expanded at comparison time using the vocabulary the model was trained against, never guessed.
settings: CPU. Pipeline defaults; DECIMER_BBOX_PAD unset, i.e. 0, which is upstream behaviour. Run as 11 separate single-document invocations and merged into one run directory, so each document could be retried without disturbing the others.
note: This is the run to read for what happens to a real document, and it is also the run that exposed a scoring bug worth more than the score. CXMolScribe emits CXSMILES: where a drawing says OMe the prediction is a dummy atom carrying the label in a |$OMe;$| extension block, because C-MAGE's vendored MolScribe deliberately declines to guess an expansion. Comparing that against a spelled-out reference SMILES is comparing two representations of the same molecule, and it can only fail — 162 of the 242 predictions here carry such a label. Expanding at comparison time doubles the measured recall without re-running anything. Read the scoring ladder before the headline: the naive number is 26.5% and it is not a measurement of this pipeline.
source: run_pipeline.py --stages 1,2,3 over benchmarks/corpus, merged by benchmarks/merge_runs.py, scored against ground_truth/pdf_manifest_expanded.json
hardware: 8-core arm64 CPU, no GPU, shared with other work at the time
precision_note: These documents draw dozens of compounds each and only the PubChem-resolvable ones were recorded, so most emitted structures have no reference to be right or wrong against. A precision figure here would measure how much of each document the ground truth covers, not how well the pipeline read it — an emitted structure absent from a partial manifest scores wrong however well it was read. Recall is unaffected: its denominator is the molecules known to be drawn, which is exactly the thing a partial manifest does know.
